posts.text:
Weeks into World War I, a German memo sketched the peace Germany would dictate after a quick win. This map shows that plan.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The Septemberprogramm was drafted on 9 September 1914 by Kurt Riezler, secretary to Chancellor Bethmann Hollweg, when Berlin expected France to be beaten fast. It was a planning memo for peace talks.

2/ In the west: Belgium would become a vassal state, Luxembourg would join the German Empire, and France would lose the Briey iron-ore region and pay an indemnity large enough to block rearmament for years.
3/ In the east: buffer states carved out of the western Russian Empire. The memo names Poland, Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania, Finland and a Baltic state. The grey zones on the map show them.
4/ Tying it together was an economic association, Mitteleuropa, led by Germany. Proposed members included France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Denmark, Austria-Hungary and Poland.
5/ The plan never took effect, since the quick victory never came. Compare it with what 1919 actually produced. Which surprises you more? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
